questions_and_answers.question: Did you know that Obama isn't the first black President, but Abraham Lincoln was the First Black President?
questions_and_answers.answer: Yes, and here’s why: He’s the first President to call himself and be called black. “Black” isn’t really a term which holds much weight in terms of genetic ancestry, because Race Is a Social Construct, [ http://www.scientificamerican.com/article/race-is-a-social-construct-scientists-argue/ ]it’s much more tied to cultural identification and self identification than to genetics. I would find it unlikely that no president before Barack Obama had some African ancestry. However, having African ancestry isn’t what makes a person black. What makes a person black is a culture which defines that person as part of a racial group by skin tone. What makes a person black is being part of a cultural, not a genetic ancestry, that passes down a specific identity. No President before Obama had that identity. So, while they may have had some genetic ties to African Americans, they weren’t black in any meaningful sense. Obama self identifies as black, and most people identify him as black as well. Howe…

questions_and_answers.question: Isn’t it racist to refer to Barack Obama as the first black president when he is half white?
questions_and_answers.answer: Yeah, that is a pet peeve of mine, so whenever somebody tells me Obama is our first black president, I answer “No. He’s white.” Of course this leads to discussion, argument, but it’s the only way to reach some people that cannot understand how ludicrous it is to talk about a person with a black father and a white mother as “black” but not equally accurate to call him “white.” If you can push it far enough you can get to the heart of the discussion, which is that the concept of race has outlived whatever meager usefulness it might have had. Time to let it go.
